Native — iOS & Android

What "native" means in Flavor DS, precisely. Two things ship: token exports a SwiftUI or Compose app compiles against, resolving the same hex the web resolves for the same axes; and a platform specification — data-platform="ios|android" — that turns the web components into the platform's chrome and metrics. Colour, contrast, spacing, type and density come from the theme axes unchanged. What differs is chrome and geometry, and every figure below is the HIG or Material 3 number.

FlavorTokens.swift

SwiftUI. FlavorTheme value type, FlavorTokens.colors(theme, scheme:), @Environment(\.flavorColors), spacing/radii/type. Typechecks against the SwiftUI SDK in scripts/test-native.mjs.

Download

FlavorTokens.kt

Jetpack Compose. FlavorTheme data class, FlavorTokens.colors(theme, dark), LocalFlavorColors, FlavorThemed . Structure-checked; not compiled here — no Kotlin toolchain on the build machine, stated rather than hidden.

Download

Both are generated by packages/tokens/native-export.mjs from the shipped flavor.css through the same cascade resolver the WCAG QA uses — 216 theme keys × 43 semantic colours × 2 schemes, byte-identical to the web. Primitives are not exported (tier rule). Media background returns a transparent surfacePage; use textOnMedia for text placed directly on a photo. Defaults: hue=brand · sat=regular · contrast=aa · bg=primary · radius=rounded · density=regular.

Platform specification

Set data-platform on any container. Each row is a --platform-* token or a component override in packages/ui/src/styles/platform.css; the source column is where the number comes from. Corner radii on a platform override the Radius axis — platform convention wins over theme there, and that is deliberate.

Dynamic type — the OS text-size setting

Both platforms let people scale text system-wide, and both scale non-linearly: small text grows the most, display text the least. Every --font-size-N / --line-height-N token multiplies by its own --type-scale-N, and @flavor-ds/ui/type-scale computes the twelve multipliers per platform and step. In every product template pick iOS or Android, then drag the text size slider: iOS walks the 12 Dynamic Type categories (xSmall → AX5, Large is default), Android the 7 font-scale positions (85% → 200%, 100% default). Below are the multipliers actually applied to six of the twelve steps.

Truncation. When scaled text no longer fits, mark the element data-fds-truncate: it gets a single-line ellipsis and — only while it actually overflows — a tooltip with the full text on hover and keyboard focus. The full text never leaves the DOM, so screen readers read it whole; the tooltip is a sighted-user courtesy, not the only place the information lives. Multi-line clamp: add data-lines and set --truncate-lines.
